socializing.chapter: Chapter I — The Toll of Five Hellos

story.default: The sun hasn't cleared the hills when you reach Alderbrook, but the village gate stands shut. Blocking it is Bram — a badger the size of a barrel, arms crossed, eyebrows like thunderheads. 'No strangers past this gate,' he rumbles. 'Not until the town knows your face.' Your heart sinks. Then Bram's stern face cracks, just slightly. 'There's a toll, and it ain't coin. Five hellos. Greet five souls on the road today — the baker at her stall, the courier on his rounds, a traveler you've never met — and each hello is a key turning in this lock. Come back at dusk with five, and I'll swing the gate wide myself.' Five greetings. Five keys. The road is waiting — and Bram is watching.

socializing.task: Have a real conversation with 2 people

story.default: Bram swung the gate wide himself, just like he promised. But Alderbrook has a second gatekeeper: Mira, who runs the Lantern Inn — and she doesn't rent rooms to strangers. 'A bed's for people, not passers-through,' she says, polishing a glass. 'Here's my price: two real conversations. Not weather talk — something true. Find two souls in this town, sit with them, and let them see you. Come back when two people know your name for real, and the corner room is yours.' Two conversations. Two keys. The inn's warm light is waiting.

socializing.chapter: Chapter III — A Seat by the Fire

story.default: Word travels fast in Alderbrook: the stranger paid Mira's price. Now comes the town's oldest tradition — the firelight moot, held every week in the square. Anyone may take a seat by the fire, but custom demands you bring something: a story, a song, or simply yourself, fully present. 'Outsiders usually watch from the edge,' says Bram, nudging you forward. 'Don't. Take the empty seat. Stay a while. Let the town see you're not passing through.' The fire is lit. Your seat is empty.

story.default: Bram finds you at dawn, turning his cap in his paws — the first time you've seen the old badger nervous. 'My daughter rides out with the merchant caravan tomorrow,' he mutters. 'Someone ought to give her a proper send-off. I've... never been good at starting such things.' He looks at you. This is the quest no one assigns: reach out first. Message, call, or walk up in person — propose the gathering, set the time, make it real. Bram can't ask. So you will.

socializing.task: Initiate one social plan and follow through

story.default: The send-off was perfect — lanterns, laughter, Bram crying into his ale where he thought no one could see. Now the town turns to you. 'You've been given a seat, a room, and a gate,' Mira says. 'Time to give something back.' In Alderbrook, belonging isn't declared; it's demonstrated. Initiate the gathering yourself — plan it, invite them, follow it through to the last goodbye. If it holds, it becomes tradition. And traditions are how strangers become kin.

Every deep-space voyage stays alive because somebody cleared one locker at a time. Today's somebody is you.'
